events.title: The first ten minutes, rebuilt — and the bug that froze the table is fixed
events.summary: The first ten minutes Median playtime on the demo was seven minutes. Four out of ten people closed it inside ten. The game wasn't too hard — people were leaving before they knew what they were building toward. This update rebuilds that first stretch, and removes a bug that could end a run outright. events.title: The demo is out — six nights, Busan to Daegu, free
events.summary: It's 1999. You owe a loan shark 200,000,000 won and you have twenty-four nights to pay it back. The demo is the first six. Two cities. Busan, then Daegu. Six nights, and every third one is a boss. Boss Kang out of Jagalchi collects 30% faster than you do, and the Hwang family in Daegu just make the hill steeper. events.title: I made a video explaining every card in the deck
events.summary: Most people who find this game have never held a Hwatu card.That is probably the biggest barrier between GO, STOP and someone actually trying it, so I sat down and made a proper beginner’s guide.Forty-eight cards.Twelve months, four cards each.No numbers, no familiar suits, and almost nothing that works the way a standard Western deck does.Instead, every month is represented by a plant or seasonal image.January is pine. February is plum blossom. March is cherry blossom. August has the full moon

events.title: The page is up — GO, STOP is coming
events.summary: Hi — I make GO, STOP. Alone, which is part of why this took a while.The store page is finally up, so I can actually talk about it.It's a roguelike deckbuilder, except instead of poker hands it runs on hwatu — Korean flower cards. If you've seen them before it was probably in a film: a folding table, cigarette smoke, money on it. That's the right image.Here's the setup. It's 1999.
